first_impression.reaction: I searched for an average and the second paragraph tells me the average is meaningless. Part of me rolls my eyes, because that's what everyone says when they don't want to give a number. But the intro is calm, no 'dream day' fluff, and it promises what sits outside a package and where we stand before we sign. Hidden costs are exactly what I'm worried about, so I'll keep going, but I'm looking for a range.

journey.quote: A single average says very little about the quote you will receive for a wedding like yours.
journey.reaction: Fair point, and honest. But I typed 'average cost' for a reason. I wanted a ballpark to show Mum and Dad, who are paying for part of this. Telling me there isn't one feels like a dodge at first.

journey.quote: Under section 35(5) of the Copyright Act 1968, a couple who pays for wedding photos owns the copyright by default, but the agreement can change that, so read the usage clause before you sign.
journey.reaction: Didn't expect that, and it's genuinely useful. As a lawyer I'd assumed the photographer owns it. Citing the actual section is the kind of thing that makes me trust the rest of the page.

journey.section: Hours of coverage and the shape of your day
journey.quote: Two quotes that look alike can hide very different hours, so read this line first.
journey.reaction: Practical. This is the trap we'd fall into comparing two PDFs at 11pm.

journey.quote: If an assistant is listed, ask whether they shoot or only carry equipment.
journey.reaction: That's an insider detail. I wouldn't have thought to ask. Good.

journey.section: What shapes a wedding photographer's quote
journey.quote: Ask whether pricing differs between peak and quieter months, or between a Saturday and a weekday, and whether a date hold requires a deposit.
journey.reaction: By now every subheading ends in 'ask whether'. It's a good list, but it's all homework handed back to us. James will say 'this is a spreadsheet, not an answer'.

journey.section: Extras that sit outside the headline package
journey.quote: The package price is the start of the conversation, not the end.
journey.reaction: This is the section I actually came for. The extras list (overtime, permits, rush editing, raw files) is exactly the hidden-cost stuff I want flagged. Still no idea whether those extras are a few hundred dollars or a few thousand, though.

journey.quote: Travel: who books and pays for flights, transfers and car hire, and in which currency the quote is written.
journey.reaction: Currency is one of my real fears and nobody mentions it. Glad it's here.

journey.quote: Backup: who replaces the photographer if a flight is cancelled or they fall ill, and whether that person is named in the contract.
journey.reaction: Yes. 'Something goes wrong and no one's accountable' is my nightmare, and this is the right question.

journey.quote: In practice, it can be difficult to get a repair, replacement or refund from an overseas business, and you should ask the consumer protection agency where the business is based whether it can help.
journey.reaction: Honest trade-off, and slightly alarming. It makes me want someone on our side who deals with overseas suppliers, which I suspect is the point. It works.

journey.quote: Through Wedded Concierge, one Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you, anywhere in the world, as your single point of contact, and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: 'Confirms inclusions in writing' is the most useful thing a planner has said to me. 'Anywhere in the world' is the usual line. And does the Advisor find the photographer, or do we? Do they use people they've worked with before, or whoever's local?

journey.quote: When a service has a major problem, you can choose to cancel the contract and get a refund, which may not be a full refund because you pay a reasonable amount for any work done so far and as expected, or keep the contract and pay a lower price that takes the problem into account.
journey.reaction: Accurate and well sourced, but this whole section is long. I'd read it; Mum would skim past it. It's more consumer-law explainer than wedding advice by this point.

journey.section: Who owns the copyright in your wedding photos
journey.quote: "private or domestic purpose" includes a portrait of family members, a wedding party or children.
journey.reaction: Quoting the Act directly rather than paraphrasing. Love it, professionally. This is the bit I'd forward to James.

journey.section: How to compare quotes in writing
journey.quote: A lower headline price with fewer hours and a slower delivery date is a different product, not a saving.
journey.reaction: Good line. The seven-step comparison is the most usable part of the article.

journey.quote: There is no single honest figure, because a national average blends very different weddings.
journey.reaction: I scrolled to the FAQ hoping the number was hiding here. It isn't. After the whole article I still can't tell my parents whether to budget five thousand or twenty-five. I get why, but it's frustrating, and 'no ranges' is exactly what makes me click back to Google.

journey.quote: Enough to cover what you actually want.
journey.reaction: That answer reads like a non-answer. Slightly glib for the question I literally asked.

unanswered_questions: Even roughly, what does a photographer cost for a destination wedding of 60 to 90 guests? A range in AUD would do. (article deliberately gives no figures)
Does a Wedded Advisor source and book the photographer, or do we find our own and the Advisor coordinates? (deferred business detail)
Does Wedded Wonderland work with photographers it already knows at each destination, or whoever is local? (deferred business detail)
How is the Wedded Advisor's own fee structured, and roughly what is it? (deferred business detail)
Is there a real wedding (venue, date) with the photographer named, so we can see a full gallery from a wedding like ours? (deferred business detail)
If the photographer's quote is in euros, does the Advisor convert or lock it in AUD, or do we carry the currency risk?

turn_offs_found.quote: There is no single honest figure, because a national average blends very different weddings.
turn_offs_found.why: Vague pricing with no ranges is one of our main turn-offs. The page is titled 'Average Wedding Photographer Cost' and never gives a figure or a range, so it doesn't answer the question that brought us here.

turn_offs_found.quote: Through Wedded Concierge, one Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you, anywhere in the world, as your single point of contact, and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
turn_offs_found.why: 'Anywhere in the world' is the generic end-to-end claim. It doesn't say whether they actually find or vet the photographer, which is what this page is about.

would_share_with: James: the 'How to compare quotes in writing' steps and the extras list, so we use the same checklist when quotes come in
Dad: the copyright section, because he'll want to print and frame things and will ask who owns the photos
Mum: probably not. She'll ask 'so how much?' and the page can't tell her

cta_reaction.quote: If photography is one of many suppliers you are lining up abroad, your Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD, and agrees the fee with you in writing before any work begins.
cta_reaction.why: 'Works in your time zone' and 'quotes in AUD' hit two of our real worries, and the tone isn't pushy, which I appreciate. But I came for a cost and left without one, there's no real wedding here, and I still don't know what the Advisor's fee looks like. I'd bookmark it and use the checklist, not enquire off this post alone.

top_3_changes: Say up front, in one line, why there's no figure and what we can do instead (for example, that Wedded Concierge can get comparable written quotes for our date). Right now the 'no number' feels like a dodge rather than a choice made for us.

Make the Concierge line specific to photography: does the Wedded Advisor find and vet the photographer, use people they know at the destination, and handle the currency, instead of 'anywhere in the world'.
Trim the consumer guarantees section or move some of it lower. The copyright part is gold, but the refund and ACCC detail makes the middle drag for anyone who isn't a lawyer.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Sophie & James (planner couple): skimmed, looked for hidden costs, currency, accountability, legal certainty and anything vague
No invented brand facts; Advisor fee, photographer sourcing, currency handling and real weddings listed as unanswered questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments (fact tags, image slots, link notes) ignored
Reacted to the no-prices decision as written, without suggesting invented figures

open_questions.question: The no-prices decision is a business call, but for this persona it hits the 'vague pricing with no ranges' turn-off. Can the intro or FAQ frame the absence of a figure as a deliberate, reader-first choice and point to a way of getting comparable quotes, without stating any numbers?
Is there an approved business fact on whether the Wedded Advisor sources and vets photographers, so the Concierge line can be specific?

assumptions: Sophie & James arrived via a Google search for 'average cost wedding photographer' during early research, no destination chosen, about 14 months out.
The absence of prices is a deliberate business decision; reacted to it honestly as a reader but did not ask for invented figures.
Business details (Advisor fee, photographer sourcing, real weddings) are deferred and not penalised as must-fix.
Read intro, takeaways, cost factors (skimmed the later ones), extras, destination section and copyright closely; skimmed consumer guarantees detail; read the comparison steps; skimmed FAQ and close.
